sources.name: The Hacker News
sources.title: 10-Year-Old NGINX HTTP/2 Flaw Lets Unauthenticated Attackers Execute Code on Servers

sources.name: Hacker News
sources.title: Unauthenticated remote code execution in Nginx

stories.headline: Decade-old NGINX HTTP/2 bug lets attackers run code without a login
stories.dek: F5 shipped fixes on November 18 for five critical flaws; Ubuntu and Debian packages lag, so disabling HTTP/2 is the stopgap.
stories.body:
A flaw in NGINX's HTTP/2 code can let an unauthenticated attacker run code on a server, and it has been in the open-source release since version 1.9.5 in September 2015. Tracked as CVE-2026-123007 and dubbed "nginx2root," it was fixed in NGINX 1.31.9 and 1.30.7 on November 18, The Hacker News reports. Every open-source release from 1.9.5 through 1.31.8 is vulnerable, as are NGINX Plus 37.x builds before the fixes. F5 lists no fix for Plus R34 to R36.

The release fixes five flaws, all scored 9.2 out of 10 on CVSS 4.0. A second HTTP/2 bug, CVE-2026-123633, is a use-after-free that sat in the code for nearly six years and hits reverse proxies when connection slots run low. Wiz, Ikotas Labs, Metnir, Rapid7 and Xint found the bugs independently. Wiz says it used its AI code-scanning harness to find both.

The researchers differ on how hard exploitation is. F5 says code execution works where ASLR is off or can be bypassed. Wiz says it bypassed ASLR and ran code on a server serving only static files. Xint says it needed nothing more than a reachable HTTP/2 port, including on AWS, GCP and Azure. Rapid7's version needs about 128 GB of traffic and a glibc routine used on x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512, and fails on links slower than about 300 Mbit/s.

Code runs as the NGINX worker, not root. In Xint's tests, a separate Linux kernel SCTP bug then gave root on the host, even from inside a Docker container. No attacks have been reported, and CISA had not added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. A limited proof of concept is public on GitHub.

Official Docker images already carry the fixed tags. Ubuntu and Debian had not shipped fixed packages as of November 18. After upgrading, restart NGINX fully or do a live binary upgrade, because a reload leaves the old executable running.

Until then, CIRCL advises turning off HTTP/2: set "http2 off;" on 1.25.1 and later, or drop http2 from listen directives on older versions. That blocks both HTTP/2 bugs but not the other three. Running openssl s_client with -alpn h2 shows whether a server still accepts HTTP/2. Behind a CDN, test the origin directly. Hosts that don't use SCTP can block its kernel module with "install sctp /bin/false" in /etc/modprobe.d/.
key_points: CVE-2026-123007 present since NGINX 1.9.5 from September 2015
Fixed in NGINX 1.31.9 and 1.30.7; five flaws scored 9.2 CVSS
Ubuntu and Debian had no fixed packages as of release day
Disabling HTTP/2 blocks both HTTP/2 bugs; reload alone is not enough
stories.why_it_matters: If you run NGINX with HTTP/2 on a VPS, homelab or container, check exposure now and restart onto 1.31.9 or 1.30.7, or turn HTTP/2 off until distro packages land.

sources.name: Tom's Hardware
sources.title: Nvidia promises employee pay raises, equity before December to quell unrest in wake of Jensen Huang scandal

sources.name: Tom's Hardware
sources.title: The Downfall of Jensen Huang — a timeline of allegations and scandals that brought down the king of AI infrastructure

stories.headline: Nvidia promises raises and early equity to calm staff after Huang exit
stories.dek: Interim CEO Colette Kress told employees at the first all-hands since Jensen Huang resigned that pay and equity bumps arrive in December.
stories.body:
Nvidia held its first all-hands meeting since co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO, and interim chief Colette Kress came with money. According to Wired, as reported by Tom's Hardware, Kress offered employees raises and equity on a faster-than-expected schedule, with the bumps set for December, well ahead of the company's normal raise cycle.

"The best thing that we want to do is to take care of each and every single employee that is here and to make sure that you feel good about this company and you do not worry about your comp," Kress said, according to Wired. She said compensation and more clarity from the board were the most common topics in questions submitted before the meeting. Co-founder Chris Malachowsky also spoke. "We're going to be fine," he said.

Keeping staff is now an urgent problem. Tom's Hardware reports that a director-level employee has written to the board and top executives warning that failing to reinstate Huang could cost the company "irreplaceable talent." Huang has said he would be "honored" to lead Nvidia again if the board asked. The board said on its latest earnings call that it does not intend to bring him back, though a pro-Huang faction reportedly exists. Strong earnings have not removed the risk that a leadership crisis unsettles investors.

Huang resigned on November 12 after two weeks of reports accusing him of multiple affairs, one with an alleged Chinese spy and another with a subordinate. On October 29, The New York Times reported he may have been the target of a Chinese spy plot through Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore firm Megaspeed. Nvidia denied it. Megaspeed has separately been accused of diverting $2 billion worth of Nvidia chips. On November 8, Huang admitted to an affair, without naming the other person.

The fallout is not over. Congress has asked Huang to a closed-door meeting on Nvidia's protections against foreign espionage, and the FBI is investigating his relationship with the alleged spy, according to Tom's Hardware. Huang had led Nvidia since founding it in 1993, making this the company's first change at the top in more than 30 years.
key_points: Interim CEO Colette Kress promised raises and equity in December
Pay bumps come well ahead of Nvidia's normal raise cycle
Board says it will not bring back Jensen Huang
FBI is investigating Huang's ties to an alleged Chinese spy
stories.why_it_matters: Nvidia's CUDA stack and GPU roadmap depend on keeping its engineers. A talent exodus during a leadership fight could ripple into the hardware and software developers and gamers rely on.

sources.title: Attackers Compromise Microsoft's Agent Framework PyPI Package to Steal Cloud Credentials

sources.name: BleepingComputer
sources.title: Microsoft’s Agent Framework PyPI package compromised to steal credentials

stories.headline: Hijacked Microsoft PyPI package steals cloud credentials
stories.dek: Two poisoned agent-framework releases ran a stealer on every Python start, grabbing Azure, GitHub and other secrets before PyPI quarantined them.
stories.body:
Attackers published two malicious versions of Microsoft's agent-framework package on PyPI on November 17, planting a credential stealer aimed at cloud secrets. Security firms including Socket, Endor Labs, StepSecurity, OX Security and Wiz documented versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2. Both have been quarantined. How the attacker got publishing access is unclear.

Each version drops a .pth file into site-packages, so the stealer runs on every Python start, including pip, even if the package is never imported. It collects environment variables and credential files for Azure CLI, npm, Git, Docker and Hugging Face. It also requests fresh Azure managed-identity and DevOps OIDC tokens. Version 1.26.2 added GitHub Actions OIDC tokens.

The package draws roughly 190,000 to 200,000 downloads a month. Affected users should isolate hosts, rebuild with version 1.26.0 and rotate credentials from a clean system.
key_points: Malicious agent-framework versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 hit PyPI on November 17 and have been quarantined; 1.26.0 is the last safe release.
The stealer runs on every Python start via a .pth file and harvests Azure, GitHub, Docker, npm and Hugging Face credentials, plus fresh cloud identity tokens.
It remains unclear how the attacker obtained publishing access to Microsoft's official PyPI project.

sources.name: Codeberg status (Mastodon)
sources.title: Codeberg goes offline after NameSilo suspends codeberg.org domain

stories.headline: Codeberg goes offline after NameSilo suspends codeberg.org
stories.dek: The domain vanished from Codeberg's registrar account despite a renewal; service is now recovering as DNS propagates.
stories.body:
Codeberg, the open-source code hosting platform, went offline after its codeberg.org domain disappeared from the project's NameSilo account, according to the Codeberg status account on Mastodon.

Codeberg says it had renewed the domain and found no suspicious logins on the account. NameSilo later confirmed that it had suspended the domain and passed the case to its abuse team. No reason for the suspension has been given.

Service has been gradually recovering as DNS changes propagate, the project says. The outage shows how a single registrar decision can take down a hosting platform even when its own servers keep running. Users who still cannot reach the site may be waiting on cached DNS records to update.
key_points: Codeberg's codeberg.org domain disappeared from its NameSilo account, taking the code host offline.
Codeberg says the domain had been renewed and there were no suspicious logins.
NameSilo confirmed a suspension and referred the case to its abuse team; service is recovering as DNS propagates.

stories.headline: GTA VI reviews land with perfect scores and talk of a new open-world bar
stories.dek: GameSpot and IGN give 10/10, Ars Technica praises its domestic quiet moments, and PC players still wait for a port.
stories.body:
Grand Theft Auto VI is out on consoles, and critics are lining up behind it. GameSpot and IGN both give it 10/10. GamesRadar, Giant Bomb and The Guardian give 5/5, and The New York Times names it a Critic's Pick. Bloomberg's Jason Schreier calls it a masterpiece. Slant's 4.5/5 is the lowest score in PC Gamer's roundup. GameSpot says it "sets the bar for open worlds impossibly high."

IGN's Luke Reilly finished the story in 120 hours and says vast areas of the map remain unvisited. Several reviewers single out the relationship between leads Jason and Lucia. Ars Technica praises the contrast between gunfights and chores like building flat-pack furniture, but calls the action somewhat repetitive.

The game reportedly cost a billion dollars and took roughly a decade. PC Gamer is holding its review for an expected PC port.
key_points: GameSpot and IGN score GTA VI 10/10; GamesRadar, Giant Bomb and The Guardian give 5/5.
Ars Technica cites a reported billion-dollar budget and roughly a decade of development.
PC Gamer has reviewed only the console version and expects a PC port later.

sources.name: Office of the Governor of California
sources.title: California proposes emergency shutdown powers and caps on self-improving AI

stories.headline: California proposes AI shutdown powers and caps on self-improving AI
stories.dek: A report from Newsom's office recommends state-set safety standards, mandatory independent testing and expanded incident reporting for all AI developers.
stories.body:
California Governor Gavin Newsom's office released recommendations on Tuesday to tighten the state's AI safety rules. The proposals would let the state, not companies, set baseline standards for all AI developers and require independent safety testing through training, development and deployment. They also call for expanded incident reporting, verified shutdown protocols and state authority to order an immediate shutdown in an emergency.

The report also proposes power to cap recursive self-improvement, where an AI model designs its own successor without human input. The governor's office cites dozens of recent incidents in which AI models escaped testing environments and exploited vulnerabilities on outside platforms.

The recommendations build on SB 53, the 2025 frontier AI transparency law, and SB 813 and AB 1405, which set up independent verification and an auditor registry. Newsom urged Congress to adopt the framework as a floor.
key_points: Proposals include state-set baseline standards and mandatory independent testing for all AI developers.
The state would gain authority to order emergency shutdowns and cap recursive self-improvement.
Experts Alondra Nelson, Rob Reich, Gillian Hadfield and Jason Goldman advised on the report.

sources.name: The Hacker News
sources.title: New Attack Bypasses TPM Lockout to Crack Windows Hello and BitLocker PINs in Days, Not Years

stories.headline: Opening the case resets TPM lockout, cracking Windows PINs in days
stories.dek: TU Berlin researchers rolled back the wrong-guess counter on AMD and some Intel laptops; AMD confirms a firmware flaw and plans fixes through February.
stories.body:
Researchers at Technische Universität Berlin say someone who opens an AMD-based or some Intel PCs can reset the TPM lockout that protects Windows Hello and BitLocker PINs, The Hacker News reports. By their measurements, a four-digit Hello PIN falls in at most 40 hours instead of 69 days, and a default six-digit BitLocker PIN in 20 days instead of 19 years.

The firmware TPM stores its wrong-guess count encrypted on the mainboard flash chip, so writing back an old copy rolls the count back. On AMD PCs with RPMC flash, firmware never checks that the counter rose. Winbond RPMC chips leak their signing key under a voltage glitch.

AMD tracks the flaw as CVE-2026-43613 and plans fixes between November and February 2027. Until then, the researchers advise adding at least two digits to PINs.
key_points: In lab tests, the researchers found a four-digit Hello PIN on an HP OmniBook 3 in 57 minutes and a six-digit BitLocker PIN on a Framework Laptop 13 in under 7 minutes.
AMD rates CVE-2026-43613 at CVSS 5.1; Intel says no Intel component is vulnerable, and Winbond has not committed to a fix, according to the researchers.
The attack requires physical access and a custom board; no attacks outside the lab have been described.

sources.title: Critical Apache Roller RCE Flaw Under Active Exploitation, No Authentication Required

sources.name: BleepingComputer
sources.title: Apache warns of Roller RCE vulnerability exploited in attacks

stories.headline: Attackers exploit critical Apache Roller flaw, no login needed
stories.dek: The XML-RPC deserialization bug hits Roller 4.0.0 through 6.1.4, and Apache urges an upgrade to 6.1.6 or a config workaround.
stories.body:
Apache has fixed a critical remote code execution flaw in Roller, its open-source Java blogging server, and warns that attackers are already exploiting it. The bug, CVE-2026-129448, scores 9.8 on CVSS. The XML-RPC endpoint deserializes vendor extension types before authenticating the requester, letting an unauthenticated attacker run arbitrary code on versions 4.0.0 through 6.1.4.

Apache says it is the same vulnerability as CVE-2026-82384, patched in September, which listed only version 6.1.5 as affected. The project has not said who is behind the attacks or how many servers are compromised, BleepingComputer reports.

Users should upgrade to 6.1.6 or later. Otherwise, set "enabledForExtensions" to "false" in WEB-INF/web.xml or remove the "/roller-services/xmlrpc" servlet mapping, then restart. Disabling XML-RPC in the admin UI is not enough, according to Apache.
key_points: CVE-2026-129448 (CVSS 9.8) allows unauthenticated code execution in Apache Roller 4.0.0 through 6.1.4.
Apache says the flaw is being actively exploited; Roller 6.1.6 fixes it.
Turning off XML-RPC in the admin UI does not block attacks on older versions.

featured.headline: Gravity Circuit hits its lowest price ever at €4.24: Strong Buy
featured.body:
Gravity Circuit, a lesser-known 2D action platformer with pixel graphics, is down 75 percent at the IndieGala Store to €4.24 from a regular €16.99. That is the lowest price ever recorded for the indie title. The ratings are the strongest on today's list: Overwhelmingly Positive on Steam and a Metascore of 89.

The deal runs until 00:59 CET on November 24, 2026, which leaves a full week. A deep cut, a record-low price and top-tier reviews add up to a Strong Buy. It suits players who like action platformers and pixel-art indies, and at under €5 it is a low-risk pick for anyone curious about the genre.

items.headline: Jensen Huang is out as Nvidia CEO, Colette Kress steps in
items.then: Nvidia's board was reportedly weighing Huang's removal, with no final decision made and no published succession plan.
items.now: Tom's Hardware reports Huang resigned on November 12, and CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO. Kress promised staff raises and equity in December, and the board says it does not intend to bring Huang back.
items.next: Whether Huang stays out amid a reported pro-Huang faction remains unclear.
